q: Parking dimension for jeepney/shuttle
n: A jeepney or shuttle parking/loading slot is at least 3.00 m × 9.00 m. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VII, Sec. 707.4.b.

q: Parking dimension for truck
n: A standard truck or bus parking/loading slot is at least 3.60 m × 12.00 m. An articulated truck needs 3.60 m × 18.00 m. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VII, Sec. 707.4.b.

q: Parking dimension for articulated truck
n: An articulated truck slot is at least 3.60 m × 18.00 m, enough for a 12.00 m container van and a long or hooded prime mover. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VII, Sec. 707.4.b.

q: Accessible parking slots shall have a minimum width of how many millimeters to ensure adequate wheelchair passage?
n: Accessible parking slots must be at least 4,000 mm wide so the adjacent pathway accommodates wheelchair passage. Source: Amended IRR of BP 344 (2024), Appendix A, Item 6.7(a).

q: A newly built shopping mall in Quezon City provides a total of 800 parking slots. Based on the Amended IRR of BP 344, Table A.6.1, how many accessible parking slots must be provided?
n: For 501 to 1,000 total slots, Table A.6.1 requires 2% to be accessible: 2% × 800 = 16. Source: Amended IRR of BP 344 (2024), Appendix A, Table A.6.1.

q: As part of the government's continuing Public Utility Vehicle Modernization Program (PUVMP), the City of Manila has begun developing a new modern jeepney terminal in Malate, intended to replace the long-standing roadside loading along Quirino Avenue. Recent news reports have highlighted DOTr's push for off-street, organized terminals, LTFRB's emphasis on route rationalization, and the Manila LGU's commitment to building properly designed transport hubs that comply with national standards. The architect's site development plan shows that the total lot area of the terminal is 2,500 square meters, but only 540 square meters of this is specifically allocated for the actual jeepney parking bays. Following the standard jeepney parking slot size required under national regulations, how many jeepney parking slots can the terminal accommodate?
n: A jeepney slot is 3.00 m × 9.00 m = 27 m². 540 m² ÷ 27 m² = 20 slots. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VII, Sec. 707.4.b.

q: Entrances with vestibules shall be provided with a level area with at least
n: The original BP 344 IRR requires a level area at least 1.50 m wide and 1.80 m deep at entrances with vestibules. The 2024 amendment raises this to 1,800 mm × 1,800 mm. Source: BP 344 IRR, Entrances; Amended IRR of BP 344 (2024), Item 1.4.

q: Grab bar heights according to BP 344
n: Handrails and grab bars at ramps and stairs are set at two heights, 0.70 m and 0.90 m above the walking surface. Source: Amended IRR of BP 344 (2024), Appendix A, Item 5.3.

q: What is the primary purpose of the required air space behind grab bars or handrails under BP 344?
o: To increase the bar's structural strength
To provide a safe, unobstructed hand grip and prevent finger entrapment
n: Wall-mounted handrails need a clear space of at least 50 mm behind them. This lets the hand wrap fully around the bar for a safe grip and keeps fingers from being caught. Source: Amended IRR of BP 344 (2024), Appendix A, Item 5.7.

q: Under the accessibility standards of Batas Pambansa Blg. 344, at what heights above the finished floor should handrails be installed along ramps and stairs to accommodate both adults and children or persons with varying reach capabilities?
n: Handrails along ramps and stairs are installed at two levels, 900 mm and 700 mm, so that adults and children or shorter users can both reach them. Source: Amended IRR of BP 344 (2024), Appendix A, Item 5.3.

q: Handrail height at fire exits
n: The Fire Code requires handrails on exit stairs to be no less than 760 mm and no more than 865 mm above the tread. Source: RIRR of RA 9514 (Fire Code, 2019), Means of Egress, Guards and Handrails, Item 4.a.

q: Switch height according to BP 344
n: The 2024 amended IRR places manual switches 900 mm to 1,200 mm on center above the floor. The older IRR used 1.20 m to 1.30 m. Source: Amended IRR of BP 344 (2024), Appendix C, Item 4.1.

q: According to the 2024 Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations of Batas Pambansa Blg. 344, what is the prescribed minimum installation height for electrical outlets measured from the finished floor line?
n: Electrical outlets are installed no lower than 450 mm from the floor to the center of the outlet. Source: Amended IRR of BP 344 (2024), Appendix C, Item 17.4.

q: Accessible toilet cubicles shall have a minimum area of
n: An accessible toilet cubicle has a minimum area of 1,800 mm × 1,800 mm. Source: Amended IRR of BP 344 (2024), Appendix C, Item 6.3(a).

q: A turning space for wheelchair users shall be provided outside water closet cubicles. It shall have a minimum dimension of
n: A turning space of at least 1,800 mm × 1,800 mm for wheelchair users must be provided outside water closet cubicles. Source: Amended IRR of BP 344 (2024), Appendix C, Item 6.3(i).

q: The maximum height of water closets should be?
n: The accessible toilet seat height is 450 mm. Source: Amended IRR of BP 344 (2024), Appendix C, Item 6.7.

q: Accessible water closet grab bars shall be installed at what height relative to the toilet seat?
o: 300 mm from the top of the toilet seat to the top of the grab bars
450 mm from the top of the toilet seat to the top of the grab bars
200 mm from the top of the toilet seat to the top of the grab bars
150 mm from the top of the toilet seat to the top of the grab bars
n: Both grab bars are installed 300 mm high, from the top of the toilet seat to the top of the grab bars. Source: Amended IRR of BP 344 (2024), Appendix C, Item 6.3.

q: Urinals should have an elongated lip or trough type; the maximum height of the lip should be?
n: Urinals are wall-hung with an elongated lip. The lip is at most 350–400 mm above the floor, with a 900 × 900 mm clear space in front. Source: Amended IRR of BP 344 (2024), Appendix C, Item 6.12.

q: What type of signage should be installed in buildings to assist persons with visual impairments in identifying rooms, facilities, and destinations independently?
n: People with visual impairments identify rooms independently through tactile and Braille signage. Signs labeling public rooms must carry tactile symbols, letters and Braille. Source: Amended IRR of BP 344 (2024), Appendix A, Items 7.8–7.9.

q: Along major circulation routes, doors must be equipped with kick plates made of durable materials. What is the required height range for these kick plates under BP 344?
n: Doors along major circulation routes have kick plates of durable material from 300 mm to 400 mm high. Source: Amended IRR of BP 344 (2024), Appendix C, Item 2.13.

q: Walkways should have a headroom of not less than
n: The original BP 344 IRR requires walkway headroom of at least 2.00 m. The 2024 amendment raises it to 2,200 mm, preferably higher. Source: BP 344 IRR (1983), Walkways; Amended IRR of BP 344 (2024), Appendix B, Item 3.11.

q: The gradient along the length of pathways, sidewalks and walkways shall be kept as level as possible. Whenever and wherever possible, sidewalks/walkways shall have a gradient not steeper than?
n: Wherever possible, sidewalks and walkways have a gradient no steeper than 1:20 (5%), with a cross gradient of at most 1:100. Source: Amended IRR of BP 344 (2024), Appendix B, Items 3.2–3.3.

q: Minimum clear width of the walkway from accessible spaces to be provided between front ends of parked cars
n: A walkway at least 1,200 mm clear must be provided between the front ends of parked cars, serving the accessible slots. Source: Amended IRR of BP 344 (2024), Appendix A, Item 6.7(b).

q: Sidewalks, walkways and pathways shall have a minimum width of how many millimeters?
n: Sidewalks, walkways and pathways must be at least 1,500 mm wide, or 1,800 mm where two wheelchairs must pass. Source: Amended IRR of BP 344 (2024), Appendix B, Item 3.4.

q: When loose materials must be temporarily stored on a pedestrian footway, BP 344 requires that they be fenced and prevented from encroaching onto the main footway by a kickboard. What is the minimum height of this kickboard, which also serves as a tapping board for the blind?
n: Loose materials stored on a footway must be fenced off with a kickboard at least 200 mm high, which also serves as a tapping board for the blind. Source: BP 344 IRR, Walkways (retained in the 2024 amended IRR).

q: A ramp is an inclined way connecting one level to another, or a sloped surface connecting two or more planes at different levels. Ramps should have a minimum clear width of
n: A ramp is a sloped surface connecting two levels, and any slope steeper than 1:20 counts as one. Accessible ramps need a minimum clear width of 1,200 mm. Source: Amended IRR of BP 344 (2024), Appendix A, Ramps.

q: Curb ramps shall have a gradient not steeper than
n: Under the 2024 amended IRR, curb ramps have a gradient no steeper than 1:15. The older IRR allowed 1:12. Source: Amended IRR of BP 344 (2024), Appendix B, Item 2.3.

q: At a vehicular drop-off point, a curb ramp is required to connect the sidewalk to the carriageway. What is the minimum clear width of this curb ramp under BP 344?
n: At drop-off points for persons with disabilities at loading bays, a curb ramp must be at least 900 mm wide. Source: Amended IRR of BP 344 (2024), Appendix B, Item 2.2.

q: Ordinarily, accessible ramps should have a gradient not steeper than
n: Accessible ramps are ordinarily no steeper than 1:12. Source: BP 344 IRR, Ramps; Amended IRR of BP 344 (2024), Appendix A, Ramps.

q: First class, premiere and air-conditioned buses shall have at least how many designated seats for disabled persons near the door?
n: First class, premiere and air-conditioned buses must have at least four designated seats for disabled persons near the door. Regular buses need five. Source: BP 344 IRR, Rule IV (Public Transportation), Item 6.2.

q: Jeepneys shall have at least how many designated seats for disabled persons?
n: Jeepneys must have at least two designated seats for disabled persons, preferably the front seats. Source: BP 344 IRR, Rule IV (Public Transportation).

q: Minimum number of designated seats for persons with disabilities near the front exit/entrance door of a passenger airplane
n: Passenger airplanes must have at least two designated seats for disabled persons near the front exit/entrance door, on a per aircraft-type basis. Source: BP 344 IRR, Rule IV (Public Transportation), Item 6.4.

q: In places of assembly where the seating capacity is 301–500, how many wheelchair seating spaces should be provided for persons with disabilities?
n: The original BP 344 IRR table requires six wheelchair seating spaces in places of assembly seating 301 to 500. Larger halls add one space per additional 100 seats. Source: BP 344 IRR (1983), Places of Assembly.

q: According to the National Building Code of the Philippines, within how many hours must excavation or other disturbances on public property be restored to their former condition, unless otherwise excluded by the Building Official?
n: Excavation or other disturbance on public property must be restored to its former condition within 48 hours, unless the Building Official excludes it. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule XI (Protection of Pedestrians and Public Property).

q: Which activity regulated by the National Building Code involves the removal of an existing building or structure and the clearing of the site in preparation for future construction?
n: Demolition is the systematic dismantling or removal of a building or structure, in whole or in part, including clearing the site. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule I, Definition of Terms.

q: Which activity involves changes in the materials used, partitioning, location or size of openings, structural parts, existing utilities and equipment, but does not increase the building's height or floor area?
n: Alteration is work that changes the materials, partitioning, openings, structural parts or utilities of a building without increasing its height or floor area. Addition does increase them. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule I, Definition of Terms.

q: Which activity involves physical changes made to buildings or structures primarily to increase their value, enhance quality, or improve aesthetic appeal?
n: Renovation is a physical change to a building to increase its value, quality and/or improve its aesthetics. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule I, Definition of Terms.

q: Which of the following best describes "conversion" in the context of building use and occupancy?
o: A modification of structural components without altering the building's function
A temporary suspension of building operations for maintenance purposes
A renovation that restores a building to its original design
A change in the use or occupancy of a building or part thereof that triggers different regulatory requirements
n: Conversion is a change in the use or occupancy of a building or part of it, which brings different code requirements. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule I, Definition of Terms.

q: The first document you need if you want to construct a building
n: A Locational (Zoning) Clearance from the zoning office comes first. The Building Official will not accept a building permit application without it. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule III, Sec. 302 (requirements for building permit).

q: A property owner has already secured zoning approval and completed the required plans and studies. Before any actual construction work may legally commence, which document must be obtained from the Office of the Building Official?
n: Once zoning clearance and plans are complete, the Building Permit from the Office of the Building Official is what legally allows construction to start. Source: NBC (PD 1096), Sec. 301.

q: A document issued by the Building Official to the owner to proceed with the construction, installation, addition, alteration, renovation, conversion, repair or other work activity of a specific structure or portions thereof
n: A Building Permit is the document the Building Official issues allowing the owner to proceed with construction, addition, alteration, renovation, conversion, repair or other work. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule I, Definition of Terms.

q: A type of permit issued by the Building Official for activities being undertaken prior to or during the processing of the building permit.
n: Accessory Permits are also issued for activities undertaken before or during the processing of the building permit, such as excavation, fencing or sidewalk construction. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule III, Sec. 302.4.b.ii.

q: A supplemental permit to the Building Permit, submitted together with the notarized Building Permit application, prepared, signed and sealed by the AOR and other professionals. The Building Permit is null and void in the absence of this permit.
n: Ancillary Permits, signed and sealed by the corresponding professionals, are submitted with the building permit application. The Building Permit is null and void without them. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule III, Sec. 302.4.a.

q: A permit issued by the Building Official for parts of the project with very special functions or use which are indicated in the plans and specifications that accompany the building permit application. These may include among others: bank and record vaults; swimming pools; firewalls separate from the structure; towers; silos; tombs, etc.
n: Accessory Permits cover accessory parts of the project with very special functions or use, such as vaults, pools, separate firewalls, towers, silos and tombs. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule III, Sec. 302.4.b.i.

q: What permit is secured when the building plans, specifications, and bill of quantities are approved?
n: A Building Permit is issued once the Building Official has approved the plans, specifications and bill of quantities. Source: NBC (PD 1096), Secs. 302–303.
